## Intro

This document goes over the steps to prepare and model *Nyctanassa violacea* eBird data, largely based on the tutorial provided by [Strimas-Mackey et al. (2023)](https://ebird.github.io/ebird-best-practices/).

The code below checks and install required packages as needed:

```{r eval=F,echo=F,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
pkgs <- c('tidyverse','rnaturalerthdata','terra','auk')
  
for (i in pkgs){
  if (!(requireNamespace(pkg,quietly = TRUE))){
    install.packages(pkg)
  }
}
```

## eBird data

First step is to import eBird data into R. Data was downloaded for three states: California, Baja California and Baja California Sur. Data comes in two formats: observations (i.e., each row is one observation for that species) and checklists (i.e., each row is an checklist for which that species was observed). Both will be used throughout this document to estimate final metrics reflecting species presence and abundance.

We will use `auk` functions `read_ebd()` and `read_sampling()` to import observations and checklists, respectively. These functions will automatically perform several data checks and format columns for downstream analyses.

> Note: The sampling dataset for California has been loaded and fully filtered separate from this code, since the file was previously too large to be stored on Github. Therefore, steps below will be done for all files except California Sampling Dataset.

```{r eval=F,echo=F,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
observations <- read_ebd('data/ebd_nyc_vio/')

samp_filt <- samp %>%
  filter(all_species_reported,
         between(year(observation_date), 2000, 2025),
         observation_type %in% c("Stationary", "Traveling"),
         duration_minutes <= 360,
         effort_distance_km <= 10,
         number_observers <= 10)
```

Perform all filters here: complete list, years (2000-2025), observation type and effort

### Proportion of records

First check of the increase in proportion of *N. violacea* records in California

- Get data for all lists in California
- Grid the area and filter only to lists that fall into checklists where *N. violacea* was observed
- Per year, count raw *N. violacea* lists / raw total lists per grid.
- Plot average temporal consecutive differences to have an idea of increase/decrease.

### Spatial sub-sampling

Create a grid for all three states and subsample a maximum number of lists per grid.
This will help correct for the fact that eBird is overall more used in the US

Then merge data from all three states
